correctness.rationale: The unnormalized Laplacian has four orthogonal invariant components with eigenvalues 0, b on A-zero-sum, a on B-zero-sum and a+b on part contrast. The signed heat-distribution difference for an A vertex x and B vertex y has positive mass at x and other B vertices and negative at y and other A vertices for t>0. Transport on graph metric has cheap cross-part cost1, costly same-part cost2; the excess imbalance forces cost2 |s_x-d_y|, giving W1=E+2 max{(a-1)(U-E)/a,(b-1)(V-E)/b}; for a>=b its first branch wins. The explicit fixed potential f(x)=2, f(other A)=0, f(all B)=1 is 1-Lipschitz and realizes this cost for all t, establishing exact dual and operator norm. Differentiating gives derivative sign [-2m(M-1)+(M-2)(M+m)e^{-Mt}]/M, with initial threshold M-m-2, a unique root only if M-m>2, and explicit t*, peak; K1,1 direct case exp(-2t). Independent original heat eigensystem plus Kantorovich dual LP for 75 graph/time combinations agrees to 3.8e-15. Tests finite, all-time result analytic.
residual_risks: Only unnormalized finite unweighted complete bipartite graphs; no claim for normalized random walks.

final_claim: For all finite unit-edge K_{a,b}, positive integer parts and unnormalized graph Laplacian, the shortest-path graph-Lipschitz seminorm of e^{-tL} is Lambda(t)=(2-2/M)e^{-mt}-(1-2/M)e^{-(M+m)t}, M=max(a,b), m=min. One fixed Lipschitz function attains it for every t. It overshoots 1 iff M-m>2; unique positive maximizer t*=(1/M)log[(M-2)(M+m)/(2m(M-1))], and sharp peak formula with limit2 at fixed m, M->infinity.
